t:
(a) In General.—The Secretary of Transportation shall carry out a pilot program at not more than 5 public-use airports under which the Federal Aviation Administration shall use funds made available under section 48101(a) to test air traffic flow management tools, methodologies, and procedures that will allow air traffic controllers of the Administration to better manage the flow of aircraft on the ground and reduce the length of ground holds and idling time for aircraft. 
    (b) Selection Criteria.—In selecting from among airports at which to conduct the pilot program, the Secretary shall give priority consideration to airports at which improvements in ground control efficiencies are likely to achieve the greatest fuel savings or air quality or other environmental benefits, as measured by the amount of reduced fuel, reduced emissions, or other environmental benefits per dollar of funds expended under the pilot program. 
    (c) Maximum Amount.—Not more than a total of $2,500,000 may be expended under the pilot program at any single public-use airport.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that a pilot program at public-use airports implies coordination with airport operators or local governments, but the text never requires or authorizes any consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, or advisory body. The Secretary alone selects the airports using statutory criteria, and the FAA tests tools for its own air traffic controllers. Every actor in the decision is inside the federal government, so this is not participation.
fable.s: The Secretary of Transportation shall carry out a pilot program at not more than 5 public-use airports

qwen_block.w: This section authorizes the Secretary of Transportation and the Federal Aviation Administration to conduct a pilot program. It specifies internal selection criteria based on efficiency and environmental benefits but does not require consultation, coordination, or participation with any outside parties (such as airport operators, airlines, or the public) in the decision-making process. All actors mentioned (Secretary, FAA, air traffic controllers) are inside the federal government.
qwen_block.s: The Secretary of Transportation shall carry out a pilot program at not more than 5 public-use airports under which the Federal Aviation Administration shall use funds made available under section 48101(a) to test air traffic flow management tools, methodologies, and procedures that will allow air traffic controllers of the Administration to better manage the flow of aircraft on the ground and reduce the length of ground holds and idling time for aircraft.

opus.w: The Secretary chooses the pilot airports alone, based on criteria in the statute, and the FAA runs the program. No outside party is consulted, sits on a panel, comments, or can challenge the decision. The airports are only the places where the pilot happens. They have no role in the federal decision, so this does not cross the federal boundary.
opus.s: In selecting from among airports at which to conduct the pilot program, the Secretary shall give priority consideration to airports at which improvements in ground control efficiencies are likely to achieve the greatest fuel savings or air quality or other environmental benefits
opus.b: **Step 1, brief analysis.** A tempting reading is that choosing "public-use airports" for the pilot brings outside parties, the airport operators, into the decision. That reading fails. The Secretary picks the airports alone, using criteria set in the statute such as fuel savings and environmental benefits. Nothing requires consulting or coordinating with airports, states, local governments, experts or the public. There is also no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking authority or right to sue. Everyone who acts in this section (the Secretary, the FAA and air traffic controllers) is inside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: The section describes a pilot program run by the Federal Aviation Administration and sets criteria for the Secretary of Transportation to select airports. It does not require consultation with, or input from, any non-federal entities (such as airport operators, airlines, or the public) in the decision-making process. All actors mentioned (Secretary, FAA) are within the federal government.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that selecting airports involves coordination with airport authorities or local governments, implying participation. However, the text only specifies criteria for the Secretary's internal decision-making process (fuel savings, emissions) and does not mandate any consultation, hearing, or input from outside parties (such as airport operators, airlines, or the public) before the selection is made. The actors involved in the decision (Secretary of Transportation, FAA) are all inside the federal government.
